items.title: Decisions page 'crash' 2026-11-11: pm-aggregator + pm-dispatch SIGTERM'd mid-session, no self-heal (Restart=on-failure treats SIGTERM as clean)

milestone.title: PM stack coherence
milestone.description: PM stack coherence epic (#1184) and its 34 child issues: one single URL, fresh data, triage-able, hierarchical.

items.body:
## Symptom

2026-11-11 ~16:03 CST: Drew reported "the front end crashed when I was using it" about the decisions page (set `decisions-2026-11-11`, #8766) while working through it on his phone.

## Timeline (all verified on the laptop, 2026-11-11)

- 21:49–22:00Z — Drew lands 18 resolutions on the page (answers, defers incl. guided, request-infos with notes/comments). Store and fleet feed agree exactly: 18 landed, none lost, none corrupt.
- 22:00:46Z — his last landed resolution (router-edge-6649 #3, request-info with note).
- 22:01:09Z — **pm-aggregator and pm-dispatch are both SIGTERM'd in the same second** (systemd: `code=killed, signal=TERM` for both). Neither restarts. Both services share an identical ExecStart command line (`bun run src/server.ts`), so a single pattern-based kill takes both at once. The sender is not identifiable from the journal (no auditd on the laptop); pm-git-sync is exonerated (it was failing on its dirty-tree guard, which fires before it touches any service).
- 22:01:32Z — the stack sentinel notices the aggregator is down; nothing restarts it.
- ~22:03Z — Drew's next interaction hits the dead backend (public origin 502 / connection refused) — the "crash" he saw. The v2 page JS itself is not the cause: it rendered and submitted correctly for all 18 of his resolutions, its inline script parses cleanly against the live set, and all question text reaches the page only through `esc()`.

## Root cause

1. Both PM services received SIGTERM and died together.
2. Their units run `Restart=on-failure`, and systemd counts SIGTERM as a *clean* exit — so the self-heal never fired. A stop nobody issued through systemctl leaves the stack down indefinitely.

## Accounting for Drew's work

- Landed and safe (18/24): census-agent-sdks #1 (info), census-link-system #1 (info), census-quota-benchmark #1 (Keep deferred), census-close-batch #1+#2, review-loop-2025 #1+#2, host-eval-3039 #1, id-engine-5536 #1, bot-autoclose-7610 #1 (deferred), joplin-7676 #1 (deferred, lean approve, guided), opencode-autocheck-10 #1 (answered) + #2 (deferred, guided) + #3 (info), open-knowledge-6435 #1, router-edge-6649 #1+#2+#3 (info, with his notes).
- Still open (6): router-edge-6649 #4, #5, #6; watch-cadence-7013 #1; gpl-uploads-5984 #1; release-3792 #1.
- Anything Drew typed but never submitted after 22:00:46Z (most plausibly a draft note on router-edge #4, the next question he was on) lived only in the browser and is unrecoverable server-side. Everything he submitted is intact.

## Fix

- Services restarted 22:06Z; board + attention verified 200; decisions page re-verified with zero-effect probes (bad token 403) and the production store byte-identical.
- systemd drop-ins: `Restart=always` for pm-aggregator + pm-dispatch, so a raw SIGTERM self-heals in seconds. (Durable home for this policy is the home-manager source that generates these units — the drop-ins under `~/.config/systemd/user/*.service.d/` carry it until the source adopts it.)
- Decisions page draft persistence (this issue's PR): in-progress answers, comments, defer picks, info notes, and bulk selections are saved to localStorage as Drew types and restored on load; recorded questions' drafts prune automatically. A dead backend or a crashed tab can never again eat typed work.
- Regression tests: draft-script wiring + parse, and `esc()` script-breakout neutralization, in `test/decisions.test.ts`.

## Follow-ups

- Identify the SIGTERM sender if it recurs — with `Restart=always` a recurrence becomes a seconds-long blip with a fresh journal trail (start/stop timestamps) instead of an outage.
- pm-git-sync has been failing every ~35s all afternoon on untracked `.bak` files in the primary checkout (its dirt guard counts untracked backups as dirt) — deploy path fragility worth its own look; not this incident's cause.

Related: #8766 (the decisions feature).
